chunk_list: VERDANT INTEROPERABILITY TEST PLAN V1.0 Objective The plan verifies that connectors at SolCentro, NEXUS, and Instituto Técnico do Norte exchange catalogues and products according to schemas, policies, and controls. Initial runs use synthetic data. Real products are enabled after privacy and security close. Environments Development supports local tests; integration connects services with synthetic data; pilot uses authorized networks and certificates. Configurations have a version and checksum. Every test states its environment. Criteria Every case contains preconditions, identity, product, operation, input, expected result, audit record, cleanup, and owner. Failures are blocking, major, or minor. An authorization error, exposure, or acceptance of a revoked certificate is blocking. Sequence It begins with health, catalogue, and authentication; continues with authorization, products, errors, and withdrawal; and ends with performance, rollback, and deletion. Test case 1 Case 1: Health. The expected result is that all services and dependencies respond. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored.

Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 2 Case 2: Catalogue. The expected result is that the consumer discovers only visible products. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 3 Case 3: Authentication. The expected result is that a valid certificate is accepted and a revoked one rejected. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 4 Case 4: Authorization. The expected result is that policy allows the correct operation and denies others. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored.

Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 5 Case 5: Hourly product. The expected result is that four intervals are aggregated with coverage. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 6 Case 6: Minimum group. The expected result is that no product is generated from fewer than three meters. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 7 Case 7: Daily product. The expected result is that hourly products form a traceable aggregate. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored.

Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 8 Case 8: Error. The expected result is that the code is stable and reveals no details. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 9 Case 9: Withdrawal. The expected result is that a withdrawn product is no longer served and retains history. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 10 Case 10: Rollback. The expected result is that the earlier version can be restored. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored.

Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 11 Case 11: Performance. The expected result is that latency and errors remain within threshold. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 12 Case 12: Cleanup. The expected result is that temporary copies are deleted and verified. It identifies the certificate, role, product, version, request, and evidence. Response, policy, and auditing are checked. The initial state is then restored. Where it depends on an undocumented condition, it is not reproducible. Test case 13 The coverage matrix links every requirement to a case. Critical controls have both an allowed and denied test. A requirement without a test remains open. Test case 14 The report records date, environment, versions, person, results, and evidence. Screenshots contain no secrets. Values used in integration are synthetic. Test case 15 Pilot entry requires zero blocking failures, closure of network, logging, rotation, and revocation controls, and approval of aggregation. Minor failures may be accepted with an owner and date. Test case 16 Case 1: Health. The expected result is that all services and dependencies respond.
